When to Clean

In general, filters should be cleaned when the pressure drop across the
 filter bank reaches 0.25 inches W.G. However, this figure may vary from
 installation to installation, depending upon the velocities encountered and
 upon the type of dust and dirt being removed from the air stream, and the
 original design conditions.

How
 to Clean

Under ordinary conditions, far - air filters may be readily cleaned with
 water . A garden hose with pressure nozzel and water pressure of 30 to 40
 psig is satisfactory. Higher pressures are desirable although pressures as
 low as 15 to 20 psig may be used but with less satisfacory results. Hot
 water will speed up the cleaning operation . A nozzle with hose adaptor is
 preferable to an ordinary pressure nozzle .

The stream of water should be directed to the dirty side of the filter so
 that the full energy of the water jet will break the dirt mass loose from
 the media and surplus water will flush the loosened dirt out through the
 herringbone - crimped channels .

When dirt loads are heavy or tenacious, or where a considerable number of
 filters are involved and economy demands a faster cleaning operation, the
 filters should be presoaked in an alkaline cleaning solution. Recommendation
 of the exact material to use should be obtained from the manufacturers of
 cleaning products. Typical alkaline cleaners are

Dry
 Compounds

Three generally
 satisfactory, inexpensive dry alkaline materials are turco no. 16, oakite
 penetrant and kelite super S. From 2 to 4 oz. Of this material should be
 used per gallon of water
SOLVENTS:

Prepared alkaline solvents are more expensive than dry compounds, and 
 usually cannot be justified except for removing contaminants having a large 
 percentage of tenacious, greasy substances .

Caution 
 : All
 of the alkaline solution should be thoroughly washed out of the filters with
 fresh water

It is not generally necessary to clean a Far-Air filter 
 so thoroughly that the bright electroplated surface of the screen media is 
 exposed. Alight residual film of discolored oil in no way changes the 
 filter's performance after it has been reoiled

It may be necessary to front-wash and back - wash
 filters that have heavy dirt and lint loads . It is not necessary to
 wash out the last traces of lint which seem to float within the media .
 However , if a large quantity of dirty lint is permitted to accumulate
 the filters may have to be oiled periodically in a highly alkaline
 solution to remove it .

A resistance temperature detector (RTD) is a resistance element , usually made of copper, and adjusted to 10
 ohms at 25 C. Operation of the RTD is based on the principle that the 
 electrical resistance of a metallic conductor varies linearly with its
temperature ( See Fig. 7 )

sections.text: Application

The RTD and its associated equipment is designed for use with generators, transformers, and other apparatus to determine winding, gas, and liquid
temperatures. The equipment consist of two parts : the switchboard equipment
which usually includes a temperature meter, test resistor, transformer switch,
and leads: and the machine equipment which usually includes the resistance
temperature detectors, leads, and terminal block with grounding connections.
Tests

A test resistance is usually provided for periodically checking the
calibration of the temperature meter. Test resistance has value of resistance
of 11.73 ohms, which corresponds to the resistance of a detector at temperature
of 70 C. A transfer switch is used to connect the temperature meter to any one
of several detectors in the machince. The design is such that the contacts are
opened and closed in proper sequence when transferring from one detector to
another. Another position connects to the calibrated test resistor to check the
temperature meter at the 70-degree point. The construction of RTD'S is shown in
Fig. 6. Each detector has three leads designated as A,B and C the resistance of
the element itself is the total resistance from A to B or A to C minus the lead
resistance B to C.
Shaft bearing insulation

The magnetic flux path of an ac generator may be sufficiently
non-uniform to cause a small ac voltage to be induced in the circuit ( one turn
1oop ) made up of the generator shaft, bearings and the generator casing. Even
though this induced voltage is small, it could cause a large ac current to flow
if some insulation were not inserted in the circuit if the current were allowed
to flow, it would cause pitting of the bearings the circuit is opened by
insulating the collector end bearing .
Test

The insulation may be checked by the following method use a 0-200 amps-low
impedance ac ammeter with a non-metallic contact, such as a carbon brush to
connect one side of the ammeter to the shaft. Connect the other side the ammeter
to the casing to obtain a measure of the current that might flow with on bearing
insulation present . Disconnect the ammeter from the casing and connect it to
the test terminal of the end shield. if, in this case, the ammeter indicates
even a small current flow, the insulation is not satisfactory and must be
replaced or repaired .

When to Clean
In general, filters should be cleaned when the pressure drop across the
 filter bank reaches 0.25 inches W.G. However, this figure may vary from
 installation to installation, depending upon the velocities encountered and
 upon the type of dust and dirt being removed from the air stream, and the
 original design conditions.
How
 to Clean
Under ordinary conditions, far - air filters may be readily cleaned with
 water . A garden hose with pressure nozzel and water pressure of 30 to 40
 psig is satisfactory. Higher pressures are desirable although pressures as
 low as 15 to 20 psig may be used but with less satisfacory results. Hot
 water will speed up the cleaning operation . A nozzle with hose adaptor is
 preferable to an ordinary pressure nozzle .
The stream of water should be directed to the dirty side of the filter so
 that the full energy of the water jet will break the dirt mass loose from
 the media and surplus water will flush the loosened dirt out through the
 herringbone - crimped channels .

وصف
A resistance temperature detector (RTD) is a resistance element , usually made of copper, and adjusted to 10
 ohms at 25 C. Operation of the RTD is based on the principle that the 
 electrical resistance of a metallic conductor varies linearly with its
temperature ( See Fig. 7 )
Fig. 
 7 Resistance temperature curve of
copper RTD (10 ohms at 25 C )
Application
The RTD and its associated equipment is designed for use with generators, transformers, and other apparatus to determine winding, gas, and liquid
temperatures. The equipment consist of two parts : the switchboard equipment
which usually includes a temperature meter, test resistor, transformer switch,
and leads: and the machine equipment which usually includes the resistance
temperature detectors, leads, and terminal block with grounding connections.
Tests
A test resistance is usually provided for periodically checking the
calibration of the temperature meter. Test resistance has value of resistance
of 11.73 ohms, which corresponds to the resistance of a detector at temperature
of 70 C. A transfer switch is used to connect the temperature meter to any one
of several detectors in the machince. The design is such that the contacts are
opened and closed in proper sequence when transferring from one detector to
another. Another position connects to the calibrated test resistor to check the
temperature meter at the 70-degree point. The construction of RTD'S is shown in
Fig. 6. Each detector has three leads designated as A,B and C the resistance of
the element itself is the total resistance from A to B or A to C minus the lead
resistance B to C.
Shaft bearing insulation
The magnetic flux path of an ac generator may be sufficiently
non-uniform to cause a small ac voltage to be induced in the circuit ( one turn
1oop ) made up of the generator shaft, bearings and the generator casing. Even
though this induced voltage is small, it could cause a large ac current to flow
if some insulation were not inserted in the circuit if the current were allowed
to flow, it would cause pitting of the bearings the circuit is opened by
insulating the collector end bearing .
Test
The insulation may be checked by the following method use a 0-200 amps-low
impedance ac ammeter with a non-metallic contact, such as a carbon brush to
connect one side of the ammeter to the shaft. Connect the other side the ammeter
to the casing to obtain a measure of the current that might flow with on bearing
insulation present . Disconnect the ammeter from the casing and connect it to
the test terminal of the end shield. if, in this case, the ammeter indicates
even a small current flow, the insulation is not satisfactory and must be
replaced or repaired .
